title: Precision policy + calibration: live-traffic benchmarking for FP8/INT8 under long-context & bursty batching
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Create a reproducible benchmarking campaign that validates accuracy and production latency/throughput for candidate quantization policies (FP8, INT8, mixed-precision fallbacks) against long-context workloads and realistic bursty traffic patterns. Deliverables: calibration pipeline config recipes, regression thresholds (perplexity and task-level), end-to-end runbook, and a decision matrix mapping latency/throughput gains to accuracy delta and risk level.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration recipes for FP8 and INT8 that are automated and stored in the calibration artifact registry
End-to-end benchmark harness that replays live-like traces with configurable microburst distributions and sequence length mixes

Clear accuracy regressions (delta) for each model-precision variant for three eval suites: LM perplexity (WikiText-103), QA EM/F1 (NaturalQuestions subset), and summarization ROUGE-L (CNN/DailyMail subset)
Performance SLO measurements: P50/P95/P99 token latency, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and warmup behavior under KV cache pressure
Decision matrix recommending: accept / accept-with-guardrail / reject for each variant and workload profile
run_steps: 1) Generate 10 live-like traces from production sampling (trace generator script: infra/trace_gen/live_sim_v2) with configurable burstiness and seq_len distributions

2) For each model baseline (FP16) and candidate quant variant (FP8-e4m3, FP8-e5m2, INT8 per-channel, INT8 per-tensor) run calibration pipeline with three sampling strategies: uniform sampling across tokens, stratified sampling by layer activation percentiles, and outlier-trim sampling (top 0.1% activations excluded)
3) Store calibration artifacts and scale factors in the calibration registry (s3://redwood-calib/artifacts/ENG-314159/)
4) Run throughput/latency harness: replay each trace at 3 QPS profiles (low: 10 qps, medium: 75 qps, burst: 300 qps) with concurrency ramp and record P50/P95/P99 and tokens/sec for 30m windows

5) Measure accuracy by running a parallel offline evaluation: compute perplexity on WikiText-103 validation partition, EM/F1 on sampled NQ queries, and ROUGE-L on summarization set; record delta vs FP16 baseline
6) Run stability test: 24-hour long-run with burst injection every 10 minutes to observe drift, memory growth, and tail-latency tail-offs
7) Produce a final report and populate the decision matrix with recommendations and associated guardrails (e.g., require fallback to FP16 if delta_perplexity > 1.5 or p99 latency > 2x baseline)
results_summary: Preliminary results (first run): FP8-e4m3 shows 1.8-2.6x throughput improvement vs FP16 at batch sizes 8-32 on A100x2, median token latency improvement 30-40% for medium QPS. INT8 per-channel gives 2.5-3.2x throughput but exhibits larger perplexity regressions on long-context tests: delta perplexity +6.2% average; FP8-e5m2 delta perplexity +1.1% and QA EM drop 0.9 points. Warmup under KV cache pressure: INT8 variants show transient 30% tail-latency spikes on the first two requests after a cache miss, attributed to quantized kernel selection path; FP8 had smaller warmup penalty (~10%). Stability run flagged a reproducible drift in one FP8 calibration recipe when using outlier-trim sampling with k=0.1% leading to a 0.8% accuracy regression on QA after sustained bursts. See artifacts and logs for full traces and metrics.
technical_decisions: Use per-channel INT8 for weights and per-tensor for activations as a default candidate; fallback to mixed FP16 for layers with >5% quantization-induced accuracy delta
Adopt FP8-e5m2 as the low-risk production candidate for long-context workloads, with guardrails triggered by QA/ROUGE deltas
Calibration sampling: use stratified sampling by activation percentiles as default; outlier-trim sampling reserved for latency-critical workloads after manual review
Introduce a runtime policy that detects KV cache cold starts and temporarily forces model to FP16 for the first N requests (configurable N=2) to avoid tail spikes for INT8 kernels
open_risks: Calibration drift when production token distribution skews (observed during stability run) — requires telemetry to detect calibration skew and automatic re-calibration triggers
Quantized kernels have different memory access patterns increasing GC-like stalls in certain microburst shapes — requires kernel-level profiling and possible micro-optimizations
Edge cases in QA/data with long spans (>=4096) show amplified accuracy loss for INT8; may need selective layer freezing to FP16
next_steps: 1) Implement detection and auto-fallback policy for cache-cold requests at runtime (ENG-319000 - follow-up engineering task)
2) Re-run calibration pipeline with expanded sampling for NQ hard examples (target 10k queries) and compare per-example delta
3) Open a perf PR to add microbench markers to the quantized kernel paths to help isolate memory stalls (PR referenced in artifacts)
4) Draft a release note and default policy proposal for runtime that maps workload profiles to accepted precision variants
